videos.titulo: What TrendShot is and how to read it

cenas.sub: What it is and how to read the chart

cenas.texto: The crossover gives the signal. The trend gives the direction.
cenas.fala: Hi, I'm Ricardo Garcia, and this is the TrendShot Bootcamp from MoreThanMoney. It's two videos. In this first one we'll understand what TrendShot is and how to read each element of the chart. TrendShot is a trend-following scalping system. It always enters in the direction the market is already moving, and it works mainly on the one-minute and five-minute charts. Before we start, one idea that runs through everything: the signal is the trigger, but it is not the decision. The decision depends on confirmations that you'll learn to validate. Let's take it one piece at a time.

itens: Video 1 · The system and each element of the chart
Video 2 · Signal, confirmations, management and routine
cenas.fala: The bootcamp has two videos. In the first, you'll understand the system, the markets it works on, and what each element on the chart means: the crossover triangle, the background histogram, the stars, the automatic structure, the 238 average, the POC and the volume. In the second, we get into the decision: the four confirmations, the entry, the stop, the target, managing the trade when a reversal star appears, when not to enter, and a routine for your session. Watch the videos in order. Each one builds on the one before.

cenas.sub: Scalping in the direction of the trend
cenas.fala: Chapter one: so what exactly is TrendShot?

itens: Always enters in the direction the market is already moving
The guide calls it pip surfing: riding the move
Trades last minutes, at most a few hours
Assets: indices like the US30, gold, BTC and forex pairs
cenas.fala: TrendShot is a scalping system that follows the trend. The idea is simple to say and takes discipline to carry out: you always enter in the direction the market is already moving. The guide calls it pip surfing, a way of riding the move while it lasts. Trades last minutes, at most a few hours. It isn't a system for holding a trade for days. As for assets, the guide points to indices like the US30, gold, on the XAUUSD pair, BTC and forex pairs. The system is the same across all of them. Each market behaves differently, and you'll learn that through practice on a demo account.

itens: A demo account with your broker
Access to TrendShot by MTM, through MoreThanMoney
One-minute and five-minute charts
A notebook or sheet for your journal
Time to be present during sessions
cenas.fala: Before we go on, here's what you need. A demo account with your broker, because everything you learn should be practised without real money first. Access to TrendShot by MTM, through MoreThanMoney. One-minute and five-minute charts, because that's where the system works. A notebook or a sheet for your journal. And time to be present during sessions, because a scalping system doesn't work well when you only glance at it. If you can't be present, TrendShot may not be your style, and that's an honest choice.

cenas.titulo: Reading the chart, piece by piece
cenas.fala: Chapter two: how to read the chart, piece by piece.

This is the chart with everything switched on, in a buy. One note I'll say only once in this bootcamp: the charts you see are illustrative. They explain the reading. They are not real results or market history. Now, what you see. The two exponential moving averages, the red twenty and the blue fifty, which cross to give the signal. The thicker orange line is the 238 average. Behind the price, the histogram columns, blue or red, and the candles that turn blue in an uptrend. The green and red horizontal lines are the automatic structure, R1 and S1. The thin orange line extending to the right is the POC. And the blue triangle marks the cross. Right after it, the indicator draws the trade box, with the entry, the stop and four targets. Let's look at each element on its own.

itens: Red 20 crosses above the blue 50: blue triangle, buy
Crosses below: red triangle, sell
Only inside the Trade Clock: 08:00 to 21:00, chart time
The cross is the trigger, not the decision
cenas.fala: The signal comes from the cross of two exponential moving averages. The red twenty and the blue fifty. When the red crosses above the blue, a blue triangle appears above the candle: that's a buy signal. When it crosses below, a red triangle appears: that's a sell signal. There's one detail in the indicator itself you should know: the triangles only appear inside the Trade Clock, from eight in the morning to nine at night, chart time. Outside that window the averages still cross, but TrendShot doesn't mark a signal. And keep this line from the guide: the cross is the trigger, not the decision. The triangle tells you something changed. The decision only exists after the confirmations, which you'll learn in the second video.

The background histogram shows direction. It's made of columns that rise up to the averages: blue while the twenty is above the fifty, red when it's below. And there's a second visual cue: with the twenty above the fifty, the candles themselves turn blue. With a blue background and blue candles, you look for buys. With a red background, you look for sells. The guide asks you to hold the trade while the colour doesn't change. Here, colour is your patience ruler. When the background changes colour, the underlying direction changed, and that counts far more than a single candle. Notice this chart is a sell: red columns, normal candles and the red triangle at the cross.

cenas.sub: Reversal warnings and where price stalls
cenas.fala: Chapter three: the stars and the automatic structure.

cenas.titulo: Warnings that move with the price
itens: Small yellow dot: short pullback (3-bar pivot)
Blue star: deeper pullback, trend unchanged (10-bar pivot)
Large star, red at a top, green at a bottom: possible reversal
They only appear once confirmed: the indicator waits for the next candles
cenas.fala: Stars are reversal warnings, and the indicator draws them in three sizes. The smallest is a yellow dot: it marks a short pullback, a three-bar top or bottom. The blue star marks a deeper pullback, ten bars, that doesn't change the trend. And the large star, red at a top or green at a bottom, appears when the pivot is twenty-five bars and the move was at least one ATR: that's the possible reversal warning. One important detail: stars only appear once confirmed, because the indicator needs the following candles to know it really was a top. That's why a star is a warning about the move, not an order. Later you'll see how the guide uses it to protect the trade.

On this chart, the red star marks the top of the rise. After it comes a sell. When the move down reaches a bottom, a green star appears, and a new rise begins. Notice that the stars aren't signals on their own. They're context, and they appear at moments when the move may be running out of steam. If you're long and a large red star appears, that's a warning to protect. If you're short and a green one appears, it's the same. The guide is clear about that, and the second video shows exactly how that protection is managed.

itens: R1 above price turns red: it's resistance
S1 below price turns green: it's support
Break: the line changes colour and swaps role
The retest is often where averages and structure work together
cenas.fala: Market structure is drawn automatically, with two lines: R1 and S1. The indicator finds them at twenty-five-bar tops and bottoms, with a move of at least one ATR. The colours tell you each line's role relative to price. A line above price turns red: it's resistance. A line below price turns green: it's support. When price breaks a resistance and closes above it, the line turns green and starts working as support. The retest of that line is often where the averages and the structure work together. It's no guarantee price stops there, but it tells you whether the path to the target is clear or has obstacles ahead.

cenas.sub: What the corner of the chart tells you
cenas.fala: Chapter four: the trend table, the 238 average, the POC and the volume.

itens: Trend table: Up or Down from M1 to D, and price above or below the POC
Thick orange line: the 238 average
Thin orange line to the right: the POC of the last 50 candles
Red Low Volume label when volume drops below half its average
cenas.fala: At the top of the chart is the trend table. The first row shows Up or Down across several timeframes, from one minute to daily, in blue or red. The second row shows whether price is above or below the POC on fifteen minutes, thirty minutes and one hour. The thick orange line is the 238 average. On the one-minute chart it equals the fifty average on the five-minute chart: it's your longest context. The thin orange line extending to the right is the POC, the price with the most volume over the last fifty candles. And in the right corner a red Low Volume label appears when the candle's volume drops below half its average. No label means volume is normal. Notice these pieces don't give signals. They give context, and that context is what you use in the confirmations.

itens: 20/50 crossover: the trigger
Background histogram: the direction
Stars: reversal and protection warnings
Structure, 238 average and POC: the context
No single piece decides on its own
cenas.fala: Let's put the pieces together, so you can see each one's job. The 20/50 crossover is the trigger: it tells you the minute-scale move has changed. The background histogram is the direction: it tells you which side you're on. The stars are reversal warnings, and they ask you to protect the trade when you're on the wrong side of a star. The automatic structure, the 238 average and the POC are the context: they tell you where the price may stall, and whether there's room to the target. No single piece decides on its own. A triangle with the background against it, or with the 238 average on the wrong side, isn't an entry. It's just a triangle. The system only makes sense when the pieces are read together.

Look at this example. The triangles flip one way and the other, the histogram changes colour several times and the averages are tangled. That's consolidation. The guide is clear: you don't take these signals. There's no wave to catch. And look at the corner: the red Low Volume label appears. Many people enter here because the chart seems to be signalling all the time, and that's exactly the mistake. A triangle in a directionless market is just another mark on the screen. Stay out, and let the next cross with a clear direction be your goal.

itens: Treating every yellow dot as an exit
Entering a zone of tangled averages
Reading only one timeframe and ignoring the table
Confusing a protection star with an exit order
cenas.fala: Before we close this video, the most common reading mistakes. First, treating every yellow dot as an exit. The guide says they appear often and tend to be only pullbacks. Second, entering a zone of tangled averages, where signals alternate from one side to the other. Third, reading only one timeframe and ignoring the trend table. And fourth, confusing a protection star with an exit order. A reversal star asks you to protect the trade. It doesn't tell you to leave. Write these mistakes in your journal when you see them, because they're the ones that cost the most to people who are learning.

cenas.fala: Remember: this is educational content, not financial advice. Trading carries risk and you can lose money. Practise first on a demo account. See you in the second video.

itens: The four confirmations, in order
Entry at the close of the cross candle
Automatic stop or at the previous structure
The indicator's four targets and managing stars
When not to enter, and the routine
cenas.fala: Welcome to the second video of the TrendShot Bootcamp. In the first one you learned to read the chart. Now we move to the decision. We'll go through the four confirmations, in order, and only then the entry, at the close of the cross candle. Then the stop the indicator draws, automatic or at the previous structure, and the four targets in the trade box. We'll also see how to manage the trade when a reversal star appears, when not to enter, and a simple routine for your session. The system is fast. Your preparation has to be even calmer.

cenas.sub: If any one fails, let it go
cenas.fala: Chapter one: the four confirmations.

itens: Trend: Up on the higher timeframes, in the table
238 average behind price
POC behind price: Above in a buy, Below in a sell
No Low Volume label
cenas.fala: Before accepting a signal, go through four confirmations. The first is trend. Look at the table and confirm the same direction on the timeframes above yours. The second is the 238 average. In a buy, the thick orange line must be below price. In a sell, above. The third is the POC. In a buy, price must be above it, and the table shows Above. In a sell, below, and it shows Below. If the POC is still ahead, make sure there's room to reach it and factor it into the targets. The fourth is volume: the red Low Volume label must not be showing. The guide says the system works best with liquidity and fast moves. And the final rule: if any of these confirmations fails, let it pass. A weak signal missed costs nothing.

Let's apply the four confirmations to a buy. The blue triangle marks the twenty crossing above the fifty. The background and candles are blue, and the table shows Up on the higher timeframes. The 238 average, the thick orange line, is below price. The POC, the thin orange line, is also below, and the table shows Above. And there's no Low Volume label in the corner. Four out of four. Notice one thing: confirmations don't guarantee the move continues. They tell you the context is on your side right now. Entering is still a step you take with the plan and the risk already worked out.

cenas.titulo: How to check the higher trend
itens: On the one-minute chart, check the five and the fifteen
On the five-minute chart, check the fifteen and the thirty
The same direction on all three; the table shows it at once
Different directions in the table: let it go
cenas.fala: The first confirmation deserves a detail. On the one-minute chart, you check the five and the fifteen. On the five-minute chart, you check the fifteen and the thirty. You want the same direction on all three. The trend table shows this at once, so you don't have to switch charts to check. If the table shows different directions on the timeframes above, let it go. You'd be trying to make a minute-scale move against an hour-scale trend, and the system doesn't recommend that fight. The larger context leads, and the small signal has to agree with it.
Chapter two: entry, stop and target.

linhas: 100 pips (200 on gold), or at the previous structure
30% and 50% of the stop distance (60% on gold)
cenas.fala: When there's a cross, TrendShot draws the trade box for twenty candles. The entry is the close of the cross candle, after you've passed the confirmations. The stop can be automatic: one hundred pips on most pairs and indices, two hundred on gold. Or it can sit at the previous structure, the support or resistance the move came from. There are four targets, measured from the stop distance. TP1 sits at thirty percent, TP2 at fifty, or sixty on gold, TP3 at one hundred percent and TP4 at one hundred and fifty. The green zone runs from the entry to the last target, the red one from the entry to the stop. And before you send the order, size the position with the risk you decided. The indicator draws the plan, but the lot size is yours.

itens: Read the direction: histogram, candle colour and table
Wait for the 20/50 cross triangle inside the Trade Clock
Check there are no stars or resistance just ahead
Pass the four confirmations
Stop, box targets and size, and only then the order
cenas.fala: Let's put the sequence in order. One: read the direction, from the histogram colour, the candles and the table. Two: wait for the cross triangle, inside the Trade Clock. Three: check there are no stars or resistance right ahead blocking the path. Four: pass the four confirmations, and only enter if they're all met. Five: use the stop and targets from the trade box and size the position. Only then does the order go to the broker. If any step fails, the trade doesn't exist, however fast the move looks.

itens: Look for the POC and R1 or S1 ahead of the entry
Earlier large stars mark where the move already stalled
Check which of the four targets fit before the obstacle
Don't change the plan mid-trade without a reason from the plan
cenas.fala: The trade box gives you four targets, but the guide also asks you to look at the path. Look for the POC and the structure line ahead of your entry. If they're in the way, price may hesitate there. Earlier large stars help you read the path, because they mark places where the move had already stalled. Check which of the four targets fit before that obstacle. If not even the first one fits, the trade is worse than the plan expected, and that's a reason to let it pass. Finally, a discipline rule: don't change the plan mid-trade without a reason that comes from the plan. Moving a target out of hope is the shortest road to a messy journal.
Chapter three: how to manage the trade when a reversal star appears.

itens: Long, and a red star appears: protect
Short, and a green star appears: protect
Protecting means moving the stop to the entry, or into profit
The star is a protection order, not an exit order
cenas.fala: This is the part of management worth memorising. If you're long and a red star appears, or you're short and a green star appears, the guide says to protect the trade. That can mean moving the stop to the entry, or into profit already. Notice the guide's wording: the star is a protection order, not an exit order. You're not closing the trade. You're taking risk off it, and letting the move continue if it continues. Many beginners close everything at the first warning, and miss the part of the move the target was waiting for. Protecting is a decision. Exiting is a different one, and you only take it when the plan calls for it.

Look at this example of a buy. The trade is running in your favour, and a red star appears on the path. It's a warning that the move may be losing strength. The guide's action is to protect: move the stop to the entry, or into profit. If the price keeps going, the trade stays protected. If the price turns, the protection is already in place, and the result is much closer to zero than it would otherwise have been. In every case, the decision was made before the star appeared. There was no panic, there was a plan.
Chapter four: when not to enter, and the time windows to avoid.

itens: Tangled averages, with signals alternating
A signal right below a resistance, with no room
Table showing different directions on the timeframes above
238 average or POC on the wrong side, with no room
A large star on the same candle as the signal
Outside the high-volume windows
cenas.fala: There are six situations where you should let it go. First: tangled averages, with signals alternating from one side to the other, which means a sideways market. Second: a signal right below a resistance, or above a support, with no room to the target. Third: the trend table shows different directions on the timeframes above. Fourth: the 238 average or the POC is on the wrong side, with no room. Fifth: a buy signal appears on the same candle as a large red star. The guide gives this case as an example of letting it go. Sixth: outside the high-volume windows, which we'll look at next. If any of these situations is on the chart, you don't have a trade.

itens: The indicator only marks signals from 08:00 to 21:00, chart time
Inside that window, the guide avoids 16:00 to 17:30 (Lisbon, winter)
And from 20:45 onwards
Check your clock: time shifts with daylight saving
cenas.fala: The indicator already has its own clock: the Trade Clock only lets triangles appear from eight in the morning to nine at night, chart time. Inside that window, the guide lists periods to avoid, when volume tends to dry up. The times are Lisbon time, in winter. Avoid four to five thirty in the afternoon. And avoid from eight forty-five in the evening onwards, and also the early hours, from four to six thirty. Always check your clock and the time set on the chart, because time differences shift through the year. This isn't a magic rule. It's a way of not trading when the move tends to be slower or more erratic.

itens: Check the direction on the timeframes above
Check the background histogram and the 238 average
Check the POC in the table and whether Low Volume shows
Check the time and the windows to avoid
Note each signal and what happened
cenas.fala: The routine before a session is short. First, you check the direction on the timeframes above, using the table. Second, you look at the background histogram and the 238 average, which tell you the context on each side. Third, you check the POC and the corner of the chart, to see whether the red Low Volume label shows. Fourth, you confirm the time, and whether you're in one of the windows to avoid. And fifth, when signals appear, you note each one in the journal, with what happened. During the session, your job is to follow the process, and not react to every triangle. TrendShot gives you many signals. You don't need all of them.

cenas.titulo: What to record for each signal
itens: Time, timeframe and direction
The four confirmations, yes or no
If you entered: entry, stop, target and size
If a star appeared, and whether you protected the trade
Did you follow the plan? One sentence on what you learned
cenas.fala: The journal is what turns TrendShot into learning, and it matters even more in a minute-scale system. For each signal, record the time, the timeframe and the direction. Then the four confirmations, one by one, with yes or no. If you entered, record the entry, the stop, the target and the size you calculated. Also record whether a star appeared and whether you protected the trade. And finally, the most important question: did you follow the plan? After a few weeks, the journal shows you at which times and on which markets you're following the process, and where you're improvising. That's your map, and no video can replace it.

We've reached the end of the TrendShot Bootcamp. Remember the essentials: the cross is the trigger, and the trend gives the direction. You only enter when the four confirmations are met, with the stop and targets from the trade box and the size worked out. And when a reversal star appears, you protect, you don't close out of fear. Do the exercises, practise on a demo account, and keep a journal from the first signal. If you have questions, bring your cases to the community and to the MoreThanMoney live sessions. I'm Ricardo Garcia. See you next time.
